source.title: On the Relation Between the Sharpest Directions of DNN Loss and the SGD Step Length
source.authors: Stanislaw Jastrzebski; Zachary Kenton; Nicolas Ballas; Asja Fischer; Yoshua Bengio; A. Storkey

record.tranche_reason: Measures how learning rate and batch size shape Hessian curvature during training, then tests whether changing updates along sharp directions changes test accuracy and measured sharpness. This is a conceptual test of factors and measured properties related to generalization, not the original claim's direct memorization comparison.
record.gate_note: Reports results on curvature, training dynamics, and test accuracy under Nudged-SGD (NSGD). The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected comparisons, adaptive optimizers, large-batch generalization gaps, dropout, or example removal. Results cited from prior work are not rows. Training/validation accuracy and curvature values in plots without recoverable numeric values are not transcribed.
record.test_reason: The study measures SGD dynamics, unscaled Hessian curvature and NSGD test accuracy. These do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps. Batch-size experiments measure curvature and optimization instability, without a fixed-epoch comparison of held-out performance that tests V5. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that SGD dynamics along sharp Hessian directions influence the optimization path, speed and final generalization. Reduced updates along these directions can accelerate optimization and produce sharper endpoints with better test accuracy under a small base learning rate, but the accuracy benefit depends on dataset and training settings. This is not a conclusion about magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a different intervention: tracks Hessian curvature along the SGD path and adapts learning rate along top eigenvectors (NSGD); mainly CIFAR-10, with additional datasets, architectures, and settings.
record.method_sensitivity: Learning rate, batch size, momentum, learning-rate schedule, architecture, dataset, NSGD γ and K, and whether batch normalization is used affect reported curvature, training stability, or generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, reducing updates along sharp Hessian directions can yield greater unscaled Hessian curvature with improved test accuracy. For Resnet-32, K=20 reaches 88% accuracy with norm 1100 versus the prose SGD baseline's 86.4% and norm 272.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unscaled Hessian curvature does not invariably rank held-out accuracy across SGD and NSGD training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: NSGD's accuracy benefit depends on the dataset: CIFAR-100 improves relative to gamma 1, whereas Fashion-MNIST and IMDB show similar accuracy for reduced-update and gamma-1 settings despite different curvature.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing updates along sharp Hessian directions has dataset-dependent effects on held-out accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger learning rates or smaller batches limit peak Hessian curvature along training; full-batch experiments also exhibit optimization instability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rate and batch size influence curvature and stability along the SGD trajectory.

record.problems: Test accuracy is reported rather than train-test gaps for most NSGD comparisons. The sharpness analysis uses Hessian spectral or Frobenius norms, not magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness compared with norm- and margin-based measures. Experiments are limited to the stated datasets and architectures; some results are figures without recoverable exact values. Several table entries report paired norm values without explaining their pairing. Generalization results are dataset-dependent.
record.rows_left_out: Rows on Hessian evolution, full-batch instability, gradient alignment, loss changes along projected sharp directions, and curvature under learning-rate/batch-size/momentum changes were not kept because they do not measure the generalization gap named by V7. Curvature and accuracy figures in Sections 3.1–3.3 and Appendix A–B provide no reliably extractable numerical row values. Appendix tables for alternate base learning rates and momentum also report test accuracy and sharpness but do not test the relation named by V7.

untested.parts: Matched natural-label and fixed-random-label training and held-out performance.
Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Controlled dropout effects on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Raw Hessian norms are a different measure.
Accuracy after removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both V7 verdicts. The Fashion-MNIST table uses Simple-CNN, not the Resnet-32 named in the second verdict. Table 1 explicitly explains every inherited paired Hessian norm as best-validation-point/final-epoch values. Section 4 states that learning-rate-0.01 runs generally reach over 99% training accuracy and loss around 0.01, so comparable training performance is partly documented; the decisive V7 mismatch remains the sharpness measure. No omitted result tests a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fit and held-out accuracy on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classifier comparisons.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under tuning.
Large-batch versus small-batch test performance at fixed epoch budgets.

No direct comparison of magnitude-aware sharpness with norm- and margin-based measures; no data-augmentation-free comparison. The study measures Hessian sharpness and test accuracy for NSGD versus SGD.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

reader_labels.condition: Resnet-32 and Simple-CNN on CIFAR-10, NSGD with γ < 1 versus SGD at η = 0.01
reader_labels.reason: NSGD endpoints have higher reported test accuracy and much larger Hessian Frobenius norms, so this is not evidence that greater sharpness necessarily means a larger train-test gap; rows R1-R3 and R12-R13.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Resnet-32 on Fashion-MNIST and CNN on IMDB
reader_labels.reason: Authors report that the generalization benefit did not carry over on these settings, including that γ < 1 on IMDB did not find a better-generalizing region; rows R16-R22.
